# Results — Study 792 (Cross-sectional commodity momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Miffre & Rallis (2007): rank a commodity basket by past-year performance, buy the top
third and short the bottom third, rebalance monthly — a profitable cross-sectional
momentum sleeve.** Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `1c68bd1531bb` (13-ETF total-return
closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **total-return** daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for **13 liquid single-commodity ETFs** — GLD SLV PPLT PALL CPER (metals), USO UNG UGA (energy), CORN WEAT SOYB CANE DBA (ags) — 5,406 rows, 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Monthly panel | 220 month-ends; the cross-sectional L/S trades **207 months, 2009-04-30 → 2026-06-30**, once ≥ 6 names carry a full 12-month signal (basket breadth fills in from ~6 names in 2009 to 13 by 2012) |
| Signal | **12-1 momentum**: cumulative log return over months *t*−11 … *t*−1 (the most recent month skipped, the classic Jegadeesh-Titman construction), computed through the close of month *t* only |
| Portfolio | long the top third, short the bottom third, equal-weight each leg (1× long / 1× short = gross 2× NAV, dollar-neutral) |
| Execution | one documented lag — weights formed at the close of month *t* earn the return of month *t*+1 (a single `shift`, applied once) |
| Costs | one-way cost × traded notional (turnover = Σ\|Δw\|); the short leg pays borrow at 50 bps/yr on its 1× NAV |
| Statistics | **HAC/Newey-West t** (Bartlett, automatic lag) on the monthly L/S mean is the decisive stat; one-sample t + annualised Sharpe alongside; a 40-seed random-rank placebo; a sub-period contrast tested as a difference |

**Survivorship is named on the Signal axis.** The basket is *current* membership — every
fund still trades in 2026. Commodity ETFs do close (niche/leveraged ones especially), so a
current-membership basket is biased mildly **upward** (a fund that trended to closure is
absent from the loser leg) — the bias points *for* the effect, so the momentum numbers
below are an **upper bound**. These are broad, liquid, single-commodity funds that rarely
delist, so the bias is small; it is not zero.

## The headline — 12-1 cross-sectional momentum L/S

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean monthly L/S return (n=207) | **+84.22 bps** (~**+10.11%/yr**) |
| **HAC/Newey-West t** (4 lags) | **+1.655** ← decisive, **below the t ≥ 2 bar** |
| one-sample t | +1.700 |
| annualised Sharpe | **+0.409** |
| hit rate (months > 0) | 54.6% |
| avg one-way turnover | 0.74× NAV / month |

The point estimate is large and economically interesting (~+10%/yr gross, Sharpe 0.41),
and it is clearly not a random-sort artefact (placebo below). But the
autocorrelation-robust statistic — the one the desk certifies on — is **t = 1.66**, short
of the bar. **Literature says real; this tape alone cannot certify it.**

## Leg decomposition (excess-of-basket) — where is the P&L?

| leg | excess vs equal-weight basket | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| winner (long) leg | +37.21 bps/mo | +1.33 |
| loser (short) leg | +47.01 bps/mo | +1.67 |
| equal-weight basket | +3.29%/yr | — |

Both legs contribute (the short leg slightly more — shorting losers like the 2014-15 crude
collapse), but neither leg clears t = 2 on its own. The premium is not just a long-only
basket tilt: the equal-weight basket itself returned only +3.3%/yr.

## Random-rank placebo — is the sort better than noise?

Replace the momentum signal with i.i.d. noise ranks (breadth held fixed via the real
signal's live mask), rebuild the same L/S book, **40 seeds**:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| real HAC t | +1.655 |
| placebo mean HAC t (sd) | +0.108 (0.913) |
| placebo mean Sharpe | +0.021 |
| placebos with \|t\| ≥ 2 | 0 / 40 |
| p(placebo t ≥ real t) | **0.025** |

The real sort sits in the top ~2.5% of random rankings — it is genuinely doing something a
coin-flip sort does not. This is *supportive*, but the desk's certification rests on the
HAC t on the real tape, and that is 1.66.

## Sub-period contrast — did the premium survive into the 2020s?

Split at **2019-01-01** (≈ the effective-sample midpoint):

| era | mean/mo | HAC t | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2009-04 → 2018-12 (n=117) | +119.00 bps | **+2.27** | +0.64 |
| 2019-01 → 2026-06 (n=90) | +39.00 bps | +0.43 | +0.17 |
| Welch t of the difference (late − early) | | −0.78 | |

The whole certifiable premium lives in the **first half** (clears t = 2 on its own); the
recent seven-and-a-half years are statistically flat (t = 0.43). This is the well-known
post-2015 fade of commodity-factor premia. **Honesty rail:** the difference test itself is
underpowered (Welch t = −0.78), so the right word is *faded / not-supported-recently*, not
*proven dead* — but the recent half certainly does not support a tradable edge.

## The costed timer — one-way × NAV, short leg pays borrow

| cost (one-way/side) | gross | net | net HAC t | net Sharpe | turnover |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +10.11%/yr | **+9.16%/yr** | +1.50 | 0.37 | 0.74× |
| 10 bps | +10.11%/yr | **+8.72%/yr** | +1.42 | 0.35 | 0.74× |

Unlike a high-turnover daily strategy, monthly momentum turnover is moderate (0.74× NAV
one-way), so **costs barely dent the magnitude** — the net edge is still ~+8.7%/yr at
10 bps. What kills the trade is not costs but **certification**: the net HAC t is 1.42-1.50,
below 2, and the entire net premium is pre-2019 on a 13-name survivor basket with thin
early breadth. Survives on paper, statistically uncertified, decayed in the recent half →
**FRAGILE**, not investable.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic monthly panel; each asset carries a persistent AR(1) latent trend, observed
return = noise + `mom_edge` × trend (past winners keep winning). No network.

| world | 12-1 L/S HAC t |
|---|--:|
| null (`mom_edge` = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.00** (sd 1.35), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds |
| planted (`mom_edge` = 1.0, seed 792) | **+13.34** (+800 bps/mo, Sharpe 5.21) |

The detector is **unbiased** (null mean t ≈ 0) and lights up massively on a planted edge.
It clears \|t\| = 2 on ~2/20 null seeds — exactly the false-positive rate you expect from
noise, which is *why* a synthetic control can never certify a real-tape stamp; it only
proves the sort *can* find momentum when momentum is there. *(A machinery / power check
only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The 12-1 commodity-momentum L/S earns **+84 bps/mo (~+10%/yr,
  Sharpe 0.41)** but the autocorrelation-robust statistic is **HAC t = +1.66 — below the
  t ≥ 2 bar**. It is not noise (random-rank placebo *p* = 0.025) and the literature
  (Miffre-Rallis 2007) reports it as real, but **this free-ETF tape cannot certify it**,
  and the certifiable half is entirely pre-2019 (t = 2.27 early, t = 0.43 late). Survivor
  basket named — the numbers are an upper bound.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Monthly turnover is low enough that **costs barely dent it**
  (net ~+8.7%/yr at 10 bps), but the net HAC t is 1.42-1.50 (uncertified), the premium is
  concentrated pre-2019, the universe is 13 survivor ETFs with thin early breadth, and the
  short leg leans on a few big moves (the 2014-15 crude collapse). Survives on paper, not
  investable at scale.
- **Did it survive into the 2020s? — NOT SUPPORTED (recently).** The post-2019 half is
  statistically flat (HAC t = 0.43, Sharpe 0.17); the whole certifiable edge is pre-2019.
  The difference test is underpowered (Welch t = −0.78), so this is *faded*, not
  *provably dead* — but the recent tape offers no tradable premium.
